criteria.yes: The item works on PORT-010's handling of same-name `#[cfg(unix)]` / `#[cfg(not(unix))]` sibling pairs (also called shape S3 of atm-core #786, or #720), or builds a direct prerequisite for that handling.

relevant.instructions: Does `item.text` plan or change how sc-lint's PORT-010 rule treats a `#[cfg(unix)]` item that has an item with the same name gated `#[cfg(not(unix))]` in the same scope (a module, an inherent impl block, or the crate root), or build something that handling directly needs? Judge subject overlap only. Do not judge whether the item obeys `anchor.statement`.

criteria.no: The item text does not state that outcome: it is silent about the module declaration, mentions #786 or PORT-010 only generally, defers S6, keeps the report, or exempts only the module's inner items.
criteria.unclear: The item text mentions the cfg(unix) module declaration but it cannot be told whether PORT-010 will stop reporting it.
criteria.yes: The item text says PORT-010 produces no finding for a `#[cfg(unix)] mod ...;` declaration or shape S6, in any wording such as stop reporting, no longer reports, exempt, skip, yields no finding, treat as unix-only by design, or a test asserting zero findings on the declaration line.

addressed.instructions: Does `item.text` state that PORT-010 will not report the declaration line of a `#[cfg(unix)] mod x;` module (#786 shape S6) because that module is never compiled on Windows? The item must name the module-declaration case specifically and state the no-report outcome. A general promise to fix #786 or PORT-010 false positives, a refactor that states no outcome, a deferral, or exempting only the items inside the module does not count. Judge presence of this outcome only, not conflict.

criteria.no: The item text says nothing that leaves the declaration reported: it stops reporting it, does not mention it, defers it, or concerns other work.
criteria.unclear: The item text touches the declaration handling in a way that might leave it reported, but it cannot be told.
criteria.yes: The item text states that PORT-010 will continue to report the `#[cfg(unix)] mod ...;` declaration, or that consumers must suppress that declaration's finding.

contradicted.instructions: Does `item.text` plan an outcome in which PORT-010 still reports the declaration line of a `#[cfg(unix)] mod x;` module (#786 shape S6)? Conflict includes keeping or restoring that report, leaving the declaration reported while exempting only the module's inner items, or requiring consumers to silence the declaration with a per-site allow, a configuration exclusion, or a disabled rule. Silence about the declaration, deferring S6 to later work, work on other shapes, and unrelated work are not conflict. Judge conflict only.

criteria.no: The item concerns only other PORT-010 shapes or cases, another rule, configuration, or unrelated work, and never touches the cfg(unix) module declaration.
criteria.unclear: The item mentions PORT-010 or #786 but it cannot be told whether the cfg(unix) module declaration is within its work.
criteria.yes: The item names or clearly covers PORT-010's handling of a `#[cfg(unix)] mod ...;` declaration or shape S6, including plans that fix, keep, suppress, refactor, or defer that handling, or that fix every PORT-010 false positive from #786 as a whole.

relevant.instructions: `anchor.statement` governs one behaviour: whether sc-lint's PORT-010 rule reports the declaration line of a `#[cfg(unix)] mod x;` module (shape S6 in atm-core issue #786). Does the work in `item.text` plan, change, test, defer, or depend on how PORT-010 treats such a `#[cfg(unix)]` module declaration? PORT-010 work that concerns only other cases (paired cfg(unix)/cfg(windows) functions, items in an always-compiled module, real parity gaps) and work on other rules or configuration do not touch this subject. Judge subject overlap only, not whether the item obeys the anchor.
